answer: At the dawn of each epoch, every agent must bind its public key to a passport-chip attestation verified by a bonded registrar against the issuing state's key. A haven ledger stores one non-transferable binding per chip number and rejects any second key for that chip, so extra identities require extra passports costing C plus a per-epoch renewal fee f. With per-epoch reward R, n identities gain n(R - C/L - f) over L epochs; this linear cost deters sybils only while R < C/L + f. Forged chips, multiple passports per person, or a captured registrar remain the lagoon where attacks concentrate.
